author: synced_reader plan, Task 6b (backup/import restore endpoint)
summary: Added the first-ever backup restore/import endpoint (POST /api/projects/{project_id}/backups/{filename}/restore): scoped recovery-into-an-existing-chapter that writes the chapter WAV + paired timing sidecar back to disk and updates the chapter DB row, so a saved backup can restore reader functionality even when the archive never contained segment-level WAVs. Never extracts to disk (only zf.read() on arcnames taken from the archive's own parsed chapter_map, never zf.namelist() enumeration); every destination path is built from trusted project_id/chapter_id via get_chapter_dir + secure_join_flat, never from the arcname string.

changes.change: Added api_restore_project_backup (POST /{project_id}/backups/{filename}/restore). Locates the backup ZIP via the same os.scandir exact-name + storage.is_safe containment pattern as api_download_saved_backup/api_delete_project_backup. For each chapter_id in bundle.json's chapter_map: skips (logs) chapters not found in this project via get_chapter(chapter_id, project_id=project_id); reads the WAV via zf.read(chapter_map[cid]['audio_path']) after a zf.getinfo() existence + 2GB size-cap check; writes it to get_chapter_dir(project_id, chapter_id) under a filename derived from the chapter's own existing audio_file_path stem (or 'chapter' fallback) with a forced .wav suffix (bundles are WAV-only); if a timing_path entry is present, reads+validates it via validate_timing_sidecar and writes it with the existing write_timing_sidecar helper only on success (invalid/corrupt/oversized sidecars are logged and skipped, never fail the whole restore); updates the chapter row (audio_status='done', audio_file_path, audio_generated_at -- taken from the restored sidecar's own audio_generated_at when one was restored, so the Task 5 staleness check passes immediately post-restore, else a fresh time.time()). Returns {status, restored_chapter_ids, skipped_chapter_ids}. Whole handler wrapped in the same try/except->500 pattern as sibling routes. New imports: get_chapter/update_chapter from ...db, get_chapter_dir from ...core.config, safe_stem from ...utils.pathing, validate_timing_sidecar/TimingSidecarValidationError from ...domain.chapters.timing, write_timing_sidecar from ...domain.chapters.timing_generator.

New file, 7 tests (TDD: confirmed all 7 fail with 405 against pre-change code via git stash, then pass green after implementation): core round-trip with no segment WAVs on disk (asserts Task 5's GET .../timing route returns 200 post-restore, proving the audio_generated_at handoff), WAV-without-timing restore, chapter-deleted-after-backup goes to skipped_chapter_ids, invalid/version-mismatched timing sidecar restores the WAV but skips the sidecar (Task 5 route still 404s after), two security tests (chapter_map referencing a non-existent arcname; chapter_map referencing a real but path-traversal-named arcname -- proves content lands only inside the chapter's own safe directory, never at the path implied by the arcname string), and a double-restore idempotency check (no duplicate files, second restore overwrites cleanly).

invariants: Restore is recovery-into-an-existing-chapter only: never creates chapter/project rows, never touches characters/speakers/queue state, never restores a chapter_id into a project other than the one that already owns it in the DB. Every archive member is read by zf.read() only (never extract/extractall); the only arcnames ever read are the exact audio_path/timing_path values already present in the parsed chapter_map for that chapter_id -- zf.namelist() is never iterated. Every write destination is constructed from trusted project_id/chapter_id via get_chapter_dir + secure_join_flat, never from any string read out of the zip.
flag_for_reviewer: No bundle_version compatibility gate was added on the read/restore side even though ProjectBackupBundleModel now carries bundle_version (Task 6a) and the owner's versioned-contracts directive calls for validation at load time -- the task's explicit step-by-step scope (02-generation-and-portability.md + the Task 6b brief) did not include a version check, so none was added rather than silently expanding scope; flagged here as a candidate follow-up for whoever owns the bundle.json contract next. Also: a chapter_id present in chapter_map, found in the project, but with no 'audio_path' key at all (chapter had no audio at backup time) is treated as a silent no-op -- it lands in neither restored_chapter_ids nor skipped_chapter_ids, since the task's given definition of skipped_chapter_ids is specifically 'not found in this project'. This is the smallest-reasonable-call reading of an underspecified case; flagging per convention rather than letting it be a silent surprise.
